utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Could Mr. Court Deputy call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-63-I, the Prosecutor versus Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I have the appearances, please? For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, Peter McCloskey and with me today is Janet Stewart, as always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For Defence? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Tjarda van der Spoel, Duty Counsel for Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we'll continue the initial appearance of the accused, Mr. Drago Nikolic, pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Mr. Spoel, could I ask you a question, please? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Of course, you may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you the Duty Judge or the so-called permanent Judge for Mr. Nikolic. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: I'm the duty counsel, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I've been sitting here for the whole day. Do you have an opportunity to discuss the indictment with your client? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Yes, I did yesterday afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Do you think your client is ready to plead today? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: I know my client is ready to plead today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me ask Mr. Nikolic. Mr. Nikolic, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to plead today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have the right to have the whole indictment read out or you may waive this right. Which way do you prefer?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no need to read out the entire indictment. I have read the indictment and I fully understand the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So I will now read the individual charges brought against you, and I will then ask you whether you plead guilty or not guilty to the specific charge. Your answer in each case may be guilty or not guilty as the case may be. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's begin. Count 1 charges you with A, genocide, punishable under Article 4(3) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal or alternatively, B, complicity in genocide, punishable under Article 4(3)(E) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well. Count 2 charges you with extermination as a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(B) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 3 charges you with murder as a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(A) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 4 charges you with murder as a violation of the laws and the customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 5 charges you with persecutions on political, racial and religious grounds as a crime against humanity, including murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, terrorising the civilian population and the destruction of personal property, punishable under Articles 5(H) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may sit down, please. May the Registrar please take the note of the plea to the counts of the indictment by Mr. Nikolic. The Registrar will be instructed to fix a date for a trial when appropriate. The accused is to remain in custody until further order. At this stage, I would like to remind the Prosecution that, pursuant to Rule 66 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, it has 30 days to disclose all the supporting materials, with the indictment. At the same time, the Defence is also advised that it will have 30 days' period for filing any preliminary motions once it has received all the supporting materials in accordance with Rule 66 of the Rules. For the expeditious preparation of the case, a Status Conference will be scheduled within 120 days from today, pursuant to Rule 65 bis (A). At this stage, are there any other matters that the Prosecution wishes to raise? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have the supporting material and it's my understanding that the Registry or OLAD is -- and Mr. Nikolic almost have a permanent lawyer and hopefully in the next few days he will have one. And it's my understanding that he would prefer that the permanent lawyer had the -- actually get the material so we don't put duty counsel at having to deal with that responsibility. Also, just to inform the Court and Mr. Nikolic, it is the Prosecution's intention to offer a motion to join all the Srebrenica accused that are now in custody, and at least one that is not in custody, and we are in the process of drafting that motion and hope to have it done in the next -- next couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your information. Mr. Spoel? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Thank you, Your Honour. It is correct that Mr. Nikolic is in the process of obtaining assigned counsel so I think it would be wise that the supporting material would be given to that counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But how soon would you please let me know that Mr. Nikolic will have a permanent lawyer? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: I understand from the Registry and from Mr. Nikolic it will be a question of about a week or two, as soon as possible, I understand. I cannot pinpoint it to a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Well, it is my hope that Mr. Nikolic could have a permanent lawyer as early as possible so that he could discuss the case with that lawyer and prepare his case. Are there any matters that you would like to raise at there stage, Mr. Spoel? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, do you have anything to complain during the past month while you were in the detention unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no complaints, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about your health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My health is excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that you have to take care of yourself, because that case might be a very long case. You may sit down. Well, I believe that's all for this initial appearance, and the hearing is adjourned.
